import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML

# Helper to compare expected old behavior for complex cases
def old_unescape_html(s):
    """Replicates the old regex behavior for comparison."""
    import re
    from target import _htmlentity_transform  # assume internal helper is importable
    if s is None:
        return None
    return re.sub(r'&([^&;]+;)', lambda m: _htmlentity_transform(m.group(1)), s)


def test_none_input():
    assert unescapeHTML(None) is None


def test_empty_string():
    assert unescapeHTML("") == ""


def test_basic_entities():
    # common HTML entities
    assert unescapeHTML("&") == "&"
    assert unescapeHTML("<") == "<"
    assert unescapeHTML(">") == ">"
    assert unescapeHTML(""") == '"'
    assert unescapeHTML("A & B < C") == "A & B < C"


def test_multiple_entities():
    assert unescapeHTML("&<>") == "&<>"
    assert unescapeHTML("Start & middle < end >") == "Start & middle < end >"


def test_no_entity_ampersand():
    # Ampersand not part of an entity should stay unchanged
    assert unescapeHTML("Fish & Chips") == "Fish & Chips"
    assert unescapeHTML("&&&&") == "&&&&"


def test_malformed_entity_missing_semicolon():
    # Missing terminating ';' should not be transformed
    assert unescapeHTML("&amp") == "&amp"
    assert unescapeHTML("Hello &world") == "Hello &world"


def test_entity_followed_by_extra_text():
    # Old behavior only transforms the entity, not the trailing text
    # Example that could be affected by the regex change
    input_str = "&foo;"
    expected = "&foo;"  # old regex transforms only '&'
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected
    # Ensure the new implementation still matches the old behavior
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == old_unescape_html(input_str)


def test_entity_with_internal_ampersand():
    # String where an ampersand appears inside what looks like an entity
    # Old regex would stop before the internal '&', new regex might over‑match
    input_str = "&&unknown;test"
    # Expected: only '&' is transformed, '&unknown;' stays as is (assuming unknown stays unchanged)
    expected = "&&unknown;test"
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == old_unescape_html(input_str)


def test_non_string_input():
    # The function asserts the type is compat_str (i.e., str); other types should raise AssertionError
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(123)
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(b"bytes")


def test_large_input():
    # Stress test with a long string containing many entities
    base = "& < > " " * 1000
    expected = ("& < > \" " * 1000).strip()
    assert unescapeHTML(base).strip() == expected
